claims.claim: Jose de Navarro installed the first successful horizontal rotary cement kiln at the Old Valley Mill in Coplay, Pennsylvania, in 1889.
claims.episode_span: Jose de Navarro changed that when he installed the first successful horizontal rotary kiln at the Old Valley Mill in Coplay, Pennsylvania
claims.supporting_quote: In 1889 Jose de Navarro, a New York entrepreneur and inventor, built the first successful rotary cement kiln just north of the Coplay Cement mills.

claims.claim: Hurry and Seaman at Atlas Portland Cement received patents in 1895 for burning pulverized coal in rotary kilns.
claims.episode_span: the real scaling step came in 1895 when engineers Hurry and Seaman at the same Atlas Portland Cement operation patented a system to burn pulverized coal directly inside the rotating tube
claims.supporting_quote: Patents were filed in 1895, describing systems with specific methods of coal firing and of clinker cooling and heat recuperation, by Hurry and Seaman of the Keystone company

claims.claim: The Old Valley Mill rotary kiln turned out an average of 200 barrels of cement a day.
claims.episode_span: The first kiln at Coplay ran on oil, but the real scaling step came in 1895 when engineers Hurry and Seaman at the same Atlas Portland Cement operation patented a system to burn pulverized coal directly inside the rotating tube.
claims.source_title: Coplay Made Cement: Cement Made Coplay Historical Marker
claims.supporting_quote: The plant, known as the Old Valley Mill, was put into production on November 8, and turned out an average of 200 barrels of cement a day under the company name Keystone Cement.
